title: Portable coverage proof bundle
description: A merge plan together with the evidence its coverage classification was derived from, so a third party can recompute the classification instead of trusting it (FR-PLAN-08). Produced by 'vlab proof-bundle <source>' and checked by 'vlab verify-proof'. The bundle is emitted to stdout and is not persisted by vcs-lab.

repository.description: Which repository the evidence came from. The lineage identity is the cross-repository identity of the canonical JSON profile, so a verifier can tell whether a bundle is even about the repository it holds.

evidence.description: The sets the coverage proof lattice is evaluated against. A verifier applies the lattice to these rather than trusting the status and proof members of each change.

targetCommits.description: Commits reachable from the target head, sorted. Backs the commit-ancestry proof.

targetChangeIds.description: Logical IDs present in target history, sorted. Backs the stable-change-id proof.

receipts.description: Reachable, accepted landing, reconciliation, and rebase receipts, with the claims that matter. Backs the receipt-commit and receipt-change-id proofs, and makes a covered change traceable to the receipt that covered it.

patchEquivalentCommits.description: Advisory patch-equivalent commits. Backs the git-patch-id-heuristic classification, which is a candidate rather than a proof.

changes.description: The complete ordered source commit range outside the physical base, with one entry per commit. Repository verification binds commit, changeId, and subject to Git history. status and proof are independently recomputed. Offline verification cannot establish that this inventory is complete.

proof.description: Coverage proof, or null for new work: commit-ancestry, receipt-commit, stable-change-id, receipt-change-id, git-patch-id-heuristic. Bundles produced before v0.12.0 may carry signed-shaped-landing-receipt where receipt-commit now appears.

integrity.description: Hash over the bundle without its own integrity and signatures members, under the canonical JSON profile. Detects editing, not fabrication: a party that can recompute the hash can also restate it, which is why verification recomputes the classification and, given a repository, the evidence.

signatures.description: Reserved by the canonical JSON profile for future detached signatures; excluded from the hash alongside integrity. No signature scheme exists yet.
